name: Synanon
tagline: A drug rehabilitation program that became a church, and then something harder.
era: Santa Monica and Marin County, California, 1958 to 1991
summary: Build Synanon's holdings to $30M in assets while keeping legal scrutiny below 70.
action.open_rehab_house.desc: Costs $8,000. Adds assets and residents, and draws attention.
action.play_the_game.desc: The group's confrontational talk circle. Raises loyalty, and paranoia with it.
codex.fall.prosecuted: In 1991 the IRS revoked Synanon's tax exemption and demanded back taxes. The organization dissolved that year.
codex.fall.violence: In October 1978 two Synanon members put a rattlesnake in the mailbox of Paul Morantz, a Los Angeles lawyer who had won a case against the group. He was bitten and survived. Founder Charles Dederich and the two members pleaded no contest in 1980.
